purpose: Strip filesystem paths from client-side JS by sending only image counts from PHP, harden error messages in 3 React components, strengthen path traversal sanitization in the admin bar cache clearing handler, and remove a redundant double-encoding escapeHtml() call.
riskRationale: All changes are defense-in-depth security hardening with backward-compatible client-side handling (normalizeImageInfo accepts both old array and new number formats). The synchronous REST response still returns raw path arrays as a minor residual leak, but the primary exposure vector (wp_localize_script) is closed. One PHP warning on fresh installs needs fixing before merge.

text: Well-structured security hardening PR that correctly addresses filesystem path exposure in wppoSettings, error message hardening in 3 components, path traversal protection, and a double-encoding bug. The core fix (sanitize_image_info_for_client) is clean and handles edge cases. Tests are updated correctly. One important PHP warning bug on fresh installs must be fixed before merge; a few minor issues (decodeURIComponent edge case, redundant check, uncovered code path, incorrect @since tag) are non-blocking.

reasoning: The important PHP warning in sanitize_image_info_for_client when wppo_img_info is an empty array (fresh install, undefined array key cascading 12 E_WARNINGs per admin page load) must be fixed before merge. The synchronous REST response path leak is notable but lower priority (authenticated admin only, not rendered in DOM). All remaining issues are minor and non-blocking.

message: sanitize_image_info_for_client() cleanly converts path arrays to counts server-side, preventing filesystem path leakage to the client entirely. Handles missing/null bucket keys via null coalescing — a model of defensive server-side sanitization.

Elegant fallback: when the client sends empty payload (no path data), the endpoint reads pending paths from the DB option. The realpath-based directory traversal validation on the server ensures paths cannot escape the ABSPATH boundary.

normalizeImageInfo remains backward-compatible — it handles both the old array-of-paths format (from synchronous API responses) and the new count-only format via the Array.isArray check, ensuring no breakage for existing API responses.

Robust path traversal protection: checks both raw path.includes('..') AND decodedPath.includes('..'), correctly catching literal, URL-encoded (%2e%2e), and double-encoded (%252e%252e) directory traversal attempts.
Removal of the double-encoding escapeHtml() call is correct — React JSX already auto-escapes all text content. The new test verifying HTML tag rendering confirms the fix.

sanitize_image_info_for_client() accesses $img_info[$bucket]['webp'] without guarding for missing top-level keys. When wppo_img_info is an empty array (fresh install with no images processed), this triggers E_WARNING: Undefined array key for each of the 6 bucket/type combinations — 12 warnings per admin page load.
suggestion: Extract the bucket-level array with a null guard before accessing nested keys, so undefined top-level keys don't produce cascading warnings.

message: The synchronous fallback path returns Img_Converter::get_img_info() which contains full filesystem path arrays in the API response. This partially defeats the PR's security goal: paths are still exposed in the REST response, albeit only to authenticated admin users (manage_options) and not rendered in the DOM.
suggestion: Apply the same count-only transformation to the synchronous response, mirroring sanitize_image_info_for_client. Convert path arrays to counts before returning.

message: decodeURIComponent(path) is called unconditionally on window.location.pathname. If the URL contains a malformed percent sequence (e.g., /foo%), decodeURIComponent throws a URIError that crashes the click handler, breaking the admin bar cache-clear button.
suggestion: Wrap decodeURIComponent in a try/catch, falling back to the raw path on error, or gate it behind a path.includes('%') check.

message: The raw path.includes('..') check is redundant with decodedPath.includes('..') on line 166, since window.location.pathname is already URL-decoded by the browser. The decoded check catches both raw and encoded traversal attempts.
suggestion: Remove the raw path.includes('..') check and keep only decodedPath.includes('..') — it covers both encoded (%2e%2e) and raw (..) traversal attempts, since the browser normalizes the pathname.

message: No test coverage for the new DB fallback behavior in optimise_image. If the fallback breaks or returns unexpected data, the error would only be caught manually.
suggestion: Add a PHP integration test or a manual test plan entry that verifies: (1) empty client payload reads pending images from DB, (2) non-empty client payload still processes sent paths, (3) the path validation loop correctly normalizes and validates DB-read paths.

message: When both $webp_images and $avif_images are empty after the DB fallback, optimise_image() still returns background: true with jobs_queued: 0, causing the client to start polling image_job_status unnecessarily.
suggestion: Add an early return when both arrays are empty after the DB fallback to avoid scheduling unnecessary polling. Set background=false so the client skips polling entirely.

message: @since 1.0.0 docblock annotation on the new sanitize_image_info_for_client() method is inaccurate — this method is introduced in the current PR, not the initial release.
suggestion: Update the @since tag to reflect the plugin version in which this method is introduced (e.g., @since 1.6.0 or whichever version this PR targets).
